newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss parliament body backs Holocaust fund.
newsitem.headline: Swiss parliament body backs Holocaust fund.

text.p: A key Swiss parliament committee on Tuesday backed proposals for a law allowing Berne to pay out unclaimed bank accounts, many left by Jews killed in the Holocaust, to Jewish groups and charities.
The lower house's foreign policy committee urged the government to pursue the bill, which the cabinet two weeks ago said it was considering as a gesture of good will towards world Jewish groups.

Under the proposal, the government would be empowered to collect Swiss bank accounts untouched since World War Two and put them into a single fund, which in turn could be paid to Jewish groups and charities such as refugee aid organisations.

The idea is part of Berne's efforts to counter criticism by world Jewish groups that neutral Switzerland profited cynically from the Holocaust, including claims that Swiss banks hoarded Jewish accounts whose owners were murdered by the Nazis.

Swiss banks turned up about 40 million Swiss francs ($28 million) in dormant accounts in a search last year, although the banks say only a small part probably came from Jews hiding their assets from the Nazis.

Berne politicians say it could take all this year to pass the fund law and payment to any group might have to wait until mid-1998, when a joint commission of Swiss bankers and Jewish groups is due to report on the scope of Holocaust accounts in Swiss banks. ($1=1.4141 Swiss Franc)
